title: customer-omega-incident-timeline-draft
content:
Objective: scratchpad for timeline + commands + error snippets + internal comms draft to CS. Personal notes — messy. DO NOT SEND without review.

Summary: Customer Omega reported high 95th percentile latency and occasional 504s on hosted route /v1/generate for a narrow workload (short prompts, streaming on). Issue surfaced after rollout of model variant `rw-model-v1.2-q4` on 2026-02-24 22:30 UTC.

Timeline (local timestamps):
- 2026-02-24 22:28 UTC: Canary rollout started (auto-rollout policy).
- 2026-02-24 22:35 UTC: First customer complaint (via CS). 95p latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.2s; some 504s observed.
- 2026-02-24 22:40 UTC: I reproduced with a curl loop (see commands). Observed intermittent grpc error code 14 and 504 upstream.
- 2026-02-24 22:50 UTC: Rolled back canary to prior variant `rw-model-v1.1-q2` — partial improvement but intermittent 500s persisted.
- 2026-02-25 01:10 UTC: Identified increased queue depth on shard-3 (GPU pool A). Hypothesis: quantized kernel path causing long tail for certain sequence lengths.
- 2026-02-25 03:05 UTC: Added temporary routing rule to avoid shard-3 for customer-omega (manual routing). Customer reports improvement but not fully resolved.

Commands tried (copy/paste):
- kubectl -n redwood logs -l app=serving-runtime --tail=200 | grep shard-3
- kubectl -n redwood exec -it serving-runtime-pod -- /bin/bash -c "ps aux | grep inference"
- redwood-cli routes list --customer=omega --json > /tmp/omega-routes.json
- curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -d '{"model":"rw-model-v1.2-q4","prompt":"hi","stream":true}'
- for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rw-model-v1.2-q4","prompt":"test"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; done

Key error snippets observed:
- ERROR grpc: received message larger than max (code=13)
- ERROR upstream read timeout (504) – upstream: "inference-pod-shard-3:8080"
- Traceback (serving-runtime): TokenLossError: KV cache index out of range at kv_cache.cc:142
- WARN serving-runtime: quant-kernel exec time spike: seq_len=64, tail=823ms

Metrics/notes:
- 95p latency for customer-omega peaked at 1.3s on 2026-02-24 22:40 UTC then down to ~300ms after routing adjustment.
- shard-3 GPU utilization at 98% with queue_depth=42 around peak.
- autoscaler did not add burst nodes due to min-reservation and quota; burst policy not triggered.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Quantized kernel regression in v1.2-q4: specific sequence lengths trigger slow path causing long-tail. Evidence: exec time spike logs and reproducible with seq_len=64.
2) KV cache corruption / index bug: TokenLossError trace seen; could cause retries and backpressure.
3) Networking/VPC MTU issue causing occasional large grpc frames to be dropped leading to grpc code 13/14 errors.
4) Autoscaler policy/quotas prevented capacity from scaling fast enough (operational).

Quick repro steps for SRE runbook:
1) Run the curl loop with model v1.2-q4 and prompt variations, capture 1000 requests, gather response times and http codes.
2) Enable verbose runtime tracing on a single canary pod: kubectl exec ... REDWOOD_LOG=trace and collect /tmp/trace.log
3) Reproduce with seq_len 32/64/128 to check the exec time distribution.
4) Attempt local dev-run of quant kernel with same model binary to profile (see github PR link).

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Manual routing to avoid shard-3 for customer-omega (reduced 95p but not eliminated).
- Rollback of canary to v1.1-qu2 briefly — partial improvement.

Next steps (priority):
- [ ] Coordinate with model-onboarding (Maya) to revert v1.2-q4 rollout globally if we confirm quant kernel regression.
- [ ] Collect pprof CPU traces from shard-3 during a high-latency window.
- [ ] Run full KV cache consistency check (Luis has script: scripts/kv_check.sh).
- [ ] Ask infra to request temporary quota bump or manual scale for GPU pool A to relieve queue.
- [ ] Prepare rollback plan for customer-facing routes and automated test to prevent rollout if 95p > 500ms.

Draft internal message to CS (do not send):
Subject: Brief update — Customer Omega latency incident (investigating)
Hi Sara (CS lead),
Quick update: we saw increased latencies and intermittent 504s for Customer Omega starting ~22:30 UTC last night after a canary of `rw-model-v1.2-q4`. We've applied a manual route change to avoid the affected shard which has reduced impact for the customer. Engineering is investigating a suspected regression in the quantized execution path and will run additional traces and KV cache checks. Next update in 2 hours or sooner if we confirm root cause.
Apology + ask: please let Customer Omega know we are actively working, offer a short mitigation (we can pin them to the previous model variant for now), and request any additional logs/trace IDs they can share.
Ethan

Suggested short customer-facing blurb (for CS to edit):
We're investigating increased generation latencies on your account that began last night. We've applied a temporary routing change which should reduce impact and we can pin you to a previous model variant if you'd like immediate stability. We're running deeper diagnostics and will update within 2 hours. Sorry for the disruption.

Notes to self: keep raw logs attached to JIRA, timestamped. Don't close until KV check passes and quant kernel repro confirmed or ruled out. If quant kernel is the culprit, coordinate with Applied ML for a patch and add rollout guard in CI.

End of scratchpad.
